subject: Ramp-and-burn capacity playcall for Brightlane private GPU pools
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlane.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helen Cho <hcho@enterprisecloud.com>
Date: 2029-05-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Capacity ask — private deployment (Brightlane PoC)

Laura —

Thanks again for the earlier call. We’re kicking off the Brightlane PoC next month and need a short-run capacity plan for a private VPC deployment. Key asks:

- Target throughput: 6k token/s sustained for 2-hour peak window, 1k token/s baseline.
- Burst tolerance: 30k tokens/min for up to 3 minutes (spiky agents).
- Network: dual-path egress to our peering; we have 40Gbps to the colo.
- Prefer on-premised racks in our DC but open to a VPC with dedicated cross-connect.

Can your team put together a "ramp-and-burn" playcall that shows: sizing, headroom math, eviction/backpressure behavior, and a brief ops checklist (warm pools, cache priming)?

Would like a 45-minute sync next Friday (May 24) if that works.

—Sanjay
Director of Platform Engineering, Brightlane AI

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-17T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — private deployment (Brightlane PoC)

Thanks Sanjay — got it. Quick clarifying questions before we size:

1) Model family & sequence length: are you using an LLaMA2-70B-ish dense model or a quantized 30B variant? Typical seq len during inference (avg / p95)?
2) How sensitive are you to tail latency vs throughput (SLOs)? Do we need 99th < 200ms for the 6k token/s sustained case?
3) Is the 40Gbps link shared with other tenant traffic in your colo? Any egress caps per tenant?

We’ll draft a ramp-and-burn calc and ops checklist — Jonas can run the kernel selection and warm-pool numbers, and Marissa will outline contractual commit options that affect reserved capacity.

I’ll tentatively book Fri 24 10:00–10:45 PT; please confirm or propose another slot.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlane.ai>
Date: 2029-05-17T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — Capacity-first notes for ramp-and-burn

Laura/Team —

Quick technical sketch for the playcall (high level):

- Assumptions: Brightlane opts for a quantized 30B variant (q4_2) with avg seq len 256 tokens and p95 512 tokens. Model runs with KV cache enabled.
- Per-GPU sustained throughput: on A100-80GB we benchmark ~1.1k tokens/s for seq256 q30B with continuous batching at moderate QPS; for seq512 this drops ~30%.
- Warm-pool warmup latency: cold start (cache miss) adds ~60–120ms per request for model load; KV priming reduces this after ~50k tokens.

Sizing recommendation for target 6k token/s sustained:
- Baseline math (seq256 avg): need ~6 GPUs at peak (6k / 1.1k ≈ 5.5). Add 25% headroom for scheduling jitter & batch inefficiencies → 7–8 GPUs.
- For p95 seq512 tail: add 2 GPUs to handle bursty large sequences without degrading 99th latency.
- Burst absorption (30k tokens/min ≈ 500 tokens/s for 60s): transient surge can be absorbed by short-lived burst workers — plan for 4 spare GPUs that can be brought up within 60–90s.

Network notes: 40Gbps should be fine if traffic is mostly text; add egress headroom for model KV syncs and registry pulls (~2–3 Gbps during cache priming).

I’ll attach a quick spreadsheet with per-GPU token curves (see ramp_and_burn_calc_v2.xlsx). We should discuss admission control thresholds (queue depth per tenant) and eviction policy: prefer soft-evict (move to queued state) for graceful degradation.

—Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlane.ai>
Date: 2029-05-17T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — commercial constraints and SLA tradeoffs

FYI — commercial items we should bake into the playcall:

- Reserved vs burst: If Brightlane takes a 12-month reserved commit for 8 vGPU equivalents (our Dedicated slab), we can offer a 15% price reduction and guaranteed warm-pool pre-alloc (no cold-start charge).
- SLA opt-in: 99.9% uptime + 99th < 300ms for sustained cases will require the 8+2 buffer Jonas suggested and a cross-connect test plan.
- Early termination: include a 60-day ramp window where we measure real runrate and adjust slab counts; this avoids oversized upfront commits.

Operational attachments: attached sla_commit_matrix.pdf and the calc spreadsheet. For the playcall, propose the following agenda:
1) Quick review of Brightlane workload profile (Sanjay) — 5m
2) Sizing math + warm-pool strategy (Jonas) — 15m
3) Network and egress validation (Laura) — 10m
4) Commercial options & next steps (Marissa) — 10m

Laura — confirm the meeting invite time and I’ll prepare a short price delta table for 8 vs 10 reserved GPU equivalents.

—Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlane.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helen Cho <hcho@enterprisecloud.com>
Date: 2029-05-17T16:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — additional network details and confirm meeting

Laura/Marissa/Jonas —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifications:
- Model: we’re starting with a proprietary 32B dense model (not quantized) for fidelity experiments; avg seq len closer to 300, p95 ~600.
- Egress: the 40Gbps is dedicated per customer but shared across workloads internally in the colo rack. We can carve a guaranteed 20Gbps for Redwood during the PoC week if needed.
- We can target the Fri 24 10:00–10:45 PT slot.

Notes on tolerance: Brightlane can tolerate higher 99th latency during experimental ramp (up to 750ms) but requires no more than 5% request failures during peak. The 60-day ramp window is acceptable.

We’ll upload our network topology to your Drive link and provide a small anonymized sample trace before the call.

—Sanjay

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-17T17:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — ACTIONS: playcall prep & deliverables

Great — thanks Sanjay. Final pre-call checklist and deliverables we’ll bring to Fri 24 10:00 PT: 

- Jonas: updated GPU curves for 32B dense (seq300/seq600 p95) and revised headroom table (attach ramp_and_burn_calc_v2.xlsx).
- Marissa: commercial deltas for 8 vs 10 reserved vGPU equivalents + draft 60-day ramp clause (attach sla_commit_matrix.pdf).
- Laura (me): network validation checklist and a short ops runbook: 
  - Cross-connect test steps
  - Warm-pool priming script & schedule
  - Admission control suggested thresholds (queue depth, backoff)

Sanjay: please drop the anonymized trace and your topology diagram into the Drive link before EOD Wed 22 so Jonas can simulate p95 behavior. Also confirm the primary contact for on-call during the PoC (ops@brightlane.ai or a named engineer).

I’ll send a calendar invite now and attach the initial artifacts so everyone can pre-read. Looking forward to it.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
